results.title: MCP Integration for agents
results.snippet:
LiveAgent exposes a built-in **MCP server** (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, [FlowHunt](https://flowhunt.io), or any other MCP-compatible client, directly with your LiveAgent account. Once connected, your own AI tools/agents can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.
![](/public/article/15103/attachment/d4zg9jnagivhdk519aexdtiwte2an09c/view)
There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client - **OAuth 2.1 (recommended)**, where the AI tool discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen, or **Bearer token**, where you generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the AI tool's configuration manually.
## Finding MCP Integration in your profile
1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select **Edit profile**.
2. In the left-hand menu, navigate to the **MCP Integration** section.
This screen shows your connection details and access tokens. Use these values to configure any MCP-compatible client:
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **MCP server URL** | https://<you

results.title: Single sign-on generic example
results.snippet:
In this example we'll show you how you can implement simple single sign-on (SSO) for any kind of PHP-based webpage/application. As a result, users of your php-based webpage/app can access LiveAgent KnowledgeBase or LiveAgent Agent panel directly through a link without going through the generic login process. Requirements - Users in php-based page/webapp must have the same e-mail address as their registered username/email in LiveAgent. - Customers in LiveAgent must be REGISTERED! You can automatically register new users in your customer portal using our APIv3 or manually through your LiveAgent customer portal page.

How does it work It is pretty simple. LiveAgent uses cookies on client side to store customer authentication info. Let's have a look how cookies look like when nobody is logged-in in the KB. We have 4 default cookies used by LiveAgent Knowledgebase for storing various application and customer-based info. Now lets login into the Knowledgebase and check the cookies again: There was a new cookie created: V_auth. and the content of visitor_la_sid was also changed. It holds the auth token of logged in user. To logout, you need to delete these two cookies or set their validity

results.title: BYOK AI in LiveAgent: Use Your Own AI Provider
results.snippet:
In LiveAgent you can connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or FlowHunt. LiveAgent adds no AI fees, no token markup and no per-resolution fees.

You pay two parties for two different things: LiveAgent for your plan, and your AI provider for the AI usage on your account, at its own prices.
| Who you pay | What for | What LiveAgent adds |
|---|---|---|
| LiveAgent | Your plan | No AI fees, no token markup, no per-resolution fees |
| Your AI provider | The AI usage on your own account, at the provider’s prices | Nothing |
Plans differ in how many AI agents you can create: 1 on Starter, 5 on Team, 50 on Business and unlimited on Enterprise. Check the [AI billing on the pricing page](https://liveagent.com/pricing/) for the current plans. LiveAgent does not publish your provider’s prices, so look up the current rates with your provider before you decide.

Start a free [30-day trial](https://liveagent.com/trial/), no credit card needed, and connect your AI provider.

results.title: Attaching Files to Tickets Using the LiveAgent API
results.snippet:
First, you need to upload your file to the LiveAgent system. You can use either of the following endpoints:
### Option A: API v1 File Upload
Use the **POST /api/files** endpoint to upload a file. For detailed information, see the [Complete API reference for file upload](https://support.liveagent.com/840770-Complete-API-reference#f6ee7d770d02e790089753359529196f).
### Option B: API v3 File Upload
Alternatively, you can use the **POST /files** endpoint in API v3. For detailed information, see the [API v3 documentation for file upload](https://support.liveagent.com/docs/api/v3/#/files/uploadFile).
**Important:** Both endpoints work for uploading files, but you must use API v1 for creating ticket messages with attachments (see Step 2 below).
## Step 2: Create a Ticket Message with the File Attachment
After uploading the file, the API response will contain a `fileid` parameter. This is a unique identifier generated by the system for your uploaded file.
Use this `fileid` in the **attachments** parameter when creating a new ticket message or note via the **POST /api/conversations/[conversationid]/messages** endpoint in API v1.
For detailed information on creating messages with attachments

results.title: AI Agents feature overview
results.snippet:
The **AI Agents** feature allows you to create reusable AI-powered agents and trigger them via [automatic rules](https://support.liveagent.com/038465-Automatic-Rules-Overview). AI agents utilize the built-in MCP server and its tools to perform various actions within your LiveAgent account. They serve as a background automation layer alongside other LiveAgent [AI-powered features](https://support.liveagent.com/150554-AI-features).

**When an** [**automatic rule**](https://support.liveagent.com/038465-Automatic-Rules-Overview)** containing the action "Run AI agent" triggers,** the system dispatches the AI agent to your [AI provider](https://support.liveagent.com/838997-AI-providers), which processes the ticket and performs [actions](https://support.liveagent.com/578762-MCP-Tools-Reference) it is allowed to do, such as tagging the ticket, resolving it, assigning it to an agent, transferring it to another department, or writing a knowledge base article out of it - all without any human intervention.
